back: The period in which at least one factor of production is fixed, so output can be changed only by varying the other factors.

front: State the **law of diminishing marginal returns**.
back: If successive units of a variable factor are added to fixed factors (technology unchanged), the marginal product of the variable factor will eventually fall.
Change in total product ÷ change in the number of workers (extra output from one more worker).

front: When MP is **above** AP, what happens to AP?
back: AP rises; MP below AP lowers AP; MP cuts AP at the maximum of AP.

front: Why do returns diminish in the short run?
back: Extra workers share fixed machines and space, so each adds less to output than the one before.
Output per unit of a factor of production in a given time, for example output per worker per day.

front: How does higher productivity affect labour cost per unit?
back: It lowers it: labour cost per unit = wage ÷ output per worker.

front: Diminishing returns versus decreasing returns to scale?
back: Diminishing returns: one variable factor added to fixed factors (short run). Decreasing returns to scale: all factors increased together (long run).
